findings.description: `metadata` defaults to a shared `{}` and `put` calls `metadata.setdefault("content-type", ...)` on it. The first put without metadata stores a guessed content type in the shared default dict, and every later put without metadata reuses that type, so e.g. a .png after a .txt is stored as text/plain. A caller-supplied dict is also mutated.
findings.suggestion: Use `metadata: dict[str,str] | None = None`, then `metadata = dict(metadata or {})` before setdefault.
findings.title: Mutable default argument is mutated by setdefault

findings.description: The metadata file is replaced before the blob is written. If writing the blob fails, the old blob stays with the new metadata (wrong content type/user metadata). Overwrites are also non-atomic as a pair, and a concurrent head() can see mismatched data.
findings.suggestion: Write the blob first, then the metadata, or clean up and restore on failure.
findings.title: Metadata written before blob; failure or key collision leaves inconsistent state

findings.description: `json.loads` on a truncated or invalid meta file raises JSONDecodeError, which is not handled. If the JSON is not an object, `.pop` fails with AttributeError. A missing-meta race between is_file and read_text can also raise FileNotFoundError.
findings.suggestion: Catch (OSError, ValueError) and fall back to {}, and verify the result is a dict.
findings.title: Corrupt or non-dict metadata file crashes head()
